# Resource: tfe_admin_smtp_settings

(Only for Terraform Enterprise) Creates, updates, and destroys Admin SMTP settings.

Requires admin token configuration. See example usage for incorporating an admin token in your provider config.

## Example Usage

```typescript
import * as constructs from "constructs";
import * as cdktf from "cdktf";
/*Provider bindings are generated by running cdktf get.
See https://cdk.tf/provider-generation for more details.*/
import * as tfe from "./.gen/providers/tfe";
class MyConvertedCode extends cdktf.TerraformStack {
  constructor(scope: constructs.Construct, name: string) {
    super(scope, name);
    /*Terraform Variables are not always the best fit for getting inputs in the context of Terraform CDK.
    You can read more about this at https://cdk.tf/variables*/
    const adminToken = new cdktf.TerraformVariable(this, "admin_token", {
      description: "An admin access token",
    });
    const hostname = new cdktf.TerraformVariable(this, "hostname", {
      default: "app.terraform.io",
      description: "The HCP Terraform or Enterprise hostname.",
    });
    new tfe.adminSmtpSettings.AdminSmtpSettings(this, "this", {
      auth: "none",
      host: "smtp.example.com",
      port: 25,
      sender: "noreply@example.com",
    });
    new tfe.provider.TfeProvider(this, "tfe", {
      hostname: hostname.stringValue,
      token: adminToken.stringValue,
    });
  }
}

```

```terraform
# With write-only password

variable "admin_token" {
  description = "An admin access token"
}

variable "hostname" {
  description = "The HCP Terraform or Enterprise hostname."
  default     = "app.terraform.io"
}

variable "smtp_password" {
  type      = string
  ephemeral = true
}

provider "tfe" {
  hostname = var.hostname
  token    = var.admin_token
}

resource "tfe_admin_smtp_settings" "this" {
  host                = "smtp.example.com"
  port                = 587
  sender              = "noreply@example.com"
  auth                = "login"
  username            = "smtp_user"
  password_wo         = var.smtp_password
  password_wo_version = 1
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `auth` (String) The authentication type. Valid values are `none`, `plain`, and `login`. Defaults to `none`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether SMTP is enabled. When enabled, all other attributes must have valid values.
- `host` (String) The hostname of the SMTP server.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password used to authenticate to the SMTP server. Required if auth is `login` or `plain`. Cannot be used with `passwordWo`.
- `passwordWo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The password used to authenticate to the SMTP server, guaranteed not to be written to plan or state artifacts. Required if auth is `login` or `plain`. Either `password` or `passwordWo` can be provided, but not both. Must be used with `passwordWoVersion`.
- `passwordWoVersion` (Number) Version of the write-only password. Used to trigger updates when the write-only password changes. Must be used with `passwordWo`. When `passwordWoVersion` changes, the write-only password will be updated.
- `port` (Number) The port of the SMTP server. Defaults to `25`.
- `sender` (String) The desired sender email address.
- `testEmailAddress` (String) The email address to send a test message to. This value is not persisted and is only used during testing.
- `username` (String) The username used to authenticate to the SMTP server. Required if auth is `login` or `plain`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the SMTP settings. Always `smtp`.



## Import

Resource tfe_admin_smtp_settings can be imported in the following format: 

```shell
# via the fixed ID 'smtp'
terraform import tfe_admin_smtp_settings.this smtp
```
